stemBlocks.value: Express 2x² + 8x + 3 in the form a(x + h)² + k by completing the square.
Think first: The x² coefficient is not 1, so factor the 2 out of the first two terms before completing the square.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p101-q05 from workbook page 101.

solutionSteps.instruction: Factor 2 out of the terms containing x, leaving the constant outside.
Complete the square inside the bracket.

contentBlocks.value: Half of 4 is 2, and (x + 2)² = x² + 4x + 4, so x² + 4x = (x + 2)² − 4

strategyBlocks.value: Take 2 out of the x terms, complete the square inside the bracket, then multiply the correction back out by 2.

whyThisWorks.value: Completing the square relies on the pattern x² + 2hx, which only appears once the leading coefficient is factored out. The correction −4 created inside the bracket is multiplied by that factor when the bracket is expanded, which is why the outside constant changes by −8 rather than −4.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to multiply the internal correction by the outside factor, giving 2(x + 2)² − 1.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to multiply the internal correction by the outside factor, giving 2(x + 2)² − 1.

commonErrors.misconception: Factoring the 2 out of the constant term as well.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Factoring the 2 out of the constant term as well.

commonErrors.misconception: Halving 8 instead of halving the 4 that remains inside the bracket.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Halving 8 instead of halving the 4 that remains inside the bracket.

examTip.value: Only factor the leading coefficient out of the x² and x terms — leave the constant where it is, and it stays out of the way until the final line.
